$doc: Content for <RoadmapList>. Six items, one horizon, each a number, a title and a gloss. Every string a reader sees lives here; the component holds no copy. THIS REPLACED A THREE-COLUMN TABLE on 1 Sep and the reason was countable rather than aesthetic: the table had fourteen cells and ELEVEN OF THEM RESTATED EARLIER SECTIONS. Its `built` column was the eight frames the reader had just walked through in section 05, and its `replaced` column was section 02's three friction beats - the deleted $replacedDoc said so in its own words, 'a callback, not new information'. Only the three milestone names were new, which is why the module read long.
$horizonDoc: THE DECK HAS TWO HORIZONS AND THE STUDY HAD ONLY EVER SHOWN ONE. Deck p23 lists three short-term priorities and four longer-term vision items. Every version of this module, through the table that shipped until 1 Sep, used the short-term column and dropped the rest. That mattered because THE VISION COLUMN IS WHAT EVIDENCES THE CLAIM THE SECTION NOW MAKES: Paul set a direction, and a direction is the vision, not the fix list. So section 06 stopped being an outcome beat and became the plan; section 05 keeps the evidence and section 08 keeps where it landed. THE COST OF THAT, STATED SO IT IS NOT RESTORED: the old caption's line 'Every feature here is on a 2019 screen' IS DEAD. Items 04 to 06 have no screens and cannot have any. A later pass that reads the first three items and reaches for that sentence would be making a claim about three items that were never built.
$orderDoc: ORDER IS THE DECK'S AND IT IS SETTLED, EXTENDED FROM THREE ITEMS TO SIX ON 1 Sep. Deck p23 lists inventory sync, then delivery date accuracy, then reduce split shipments in the short-term column, then the four longer-term items in the order carried here. Paul confirmed the first three on 25 Aug and supplied the six-item sequence on 31 Aug as his own de-duplication of the deck, WHICH LISTS 'Reduce split shipments' IN BOTH COLUMNS. Do not restore the duplicate and do not reorder. THE STANDING CONSTRAINT IS UNCHANGED AND STILL APPLIES AT SIX: the sequence is settled, the REASONING for it is not, so no caption gains a why-this-order clause. An ordering a reader can see is not the same as an ordering the study has earned the right to explain.
$nameDoc: ITEM 06 DROPS THE DECK'S TRAILING & "Shop My Store", AND THE NAME IS NOT LOST - the gloss says 'her store', which is the same capability in plain language rather than as an internal product name. THE RULE IS THAT A PROPER NOUN NEEDS A REFERENT ON THE PAGE. Every other item here is self-describing, so a reader parses it cold; an internal codename with no picture beside it reads as insider shorthand. IT ALSO DISSOLVES A PROVENANCE PROBLEM RATHER THAN DEFERRING IT. The deck lists Shop My Store as unbuilt longer-term vision, while store--ribbon.png is a 2019 capture whose own button reads Shop Your Store. Either it shipped after the deck or that screen is a design, and NOBODY KNOWS WHICH. With the name off the page there is no contradiction to resolve. THE PAIRING IS THE RULE: IF THE BAND COMES BACK, THE NAME COMES BACK WITH IT. No image, no name. Neither half is reversible on its own, and that is why this is recorded beside the content rather than in a commit message.
$captionDoc: THE GLOSS SCOPES THE LIST AND MUST NOT BE SOFTENED. Three of the six were never built, and a reader given no marker assumes all six shipped. IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT REPEAT SECTION 08, which already says 'I left URBN that November. Most of what shipped, shipped without me, and I will not claim the execution.' Two statements of one caveat two sections apart reads as defensive. 06 SCOPES THE LIST; 08 SCOPES THE STUDY. NOTE WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM: that the teams kept building after Paul left. He has not said he knows that, so the study does not say it. EVERY GLOSS IS WRITTEN AS WHAT THE ITEM DOES, NEVER AS WHAT SHIPPED. That is what lets six items sit in one horizon without any of them claiming execution, and a gloss drifting into past tense during an edit would start making the claim section 08 explicitly refuses. Checked mechanically, not by eye.
